purpose: Separate gesturing pectoral fin from normal toothy face; preserve source action.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Draw one polished shark game sprite. Image 1 is the exact original SLEVEJM2 001 pose. Image 2 is corrected shark continuity reference: normal toothy head above a SEPARATE gesturing pectoral fin. Image 3 is the established shark design: neutral medium gray, pale ivory underside, black outlines, gill slits, sly heavy brows and razor triangular teeth. Match Image 1 silhouette, facing, visible limbs and waterline. Pose: Body leans diagonally up-right. The far pectoral fin reaches diagonally upward-right, its tip high near face level. Near pectoral fin hangs along gray flank. Dorsal fin extends back-left. Compact head and toothy mouth face right, mouth slightly open with a little red interior. Critical anatomy: the long rightward projection in Image 1 is a PECTORAL FIN ATTACHED AT CHEST BELOW THE JAW. It is separate from the small toothy mouth. Keep a normal compact jaw ending beneath upper snout; no long chin, beak or nostril on fin. Body shows mostly gray back/flank, with a narrow ivory belly edge at right. Two pectoral fins total: near fin down flank and far fin gesturing forward. One dorsal fin behind; do not add forehead fin, horns, tail, hands or legs. Image 2 is identity/anatomy guidance only; use exact original gesture and body lean, not its pose. Sneaky amused expression, not angry or innocent. Smooth bold black ink, restrained cel shading. Only thin cyan-white water ripples at original cutoff. All submerged anatomy absent. All contours inside canvas, clear transparent margins. Actual transparent RGBA; no checkerboard, scenery, glow, ground shadow, text or collage.
